en: The Perfection of Wisdom in Few Syllables. Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas!

Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagṛha on Vulture Peak Mountain, together with a great saṅgha of twelve thousand five hundred bhikṣus, and together with hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas.
Surrounded and honored by many thousands of millions of billions of deities, beginning with the World Protectors, he dwelt upon the glorious lion throne.

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Āryāvalokiteśvara, rising from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee upon the ground, and bowing with palms joined toward the Blessed One,
spoke these words to the Blessed One with a smiling countenance: "May the Blessed One teach the Perfection of Wisdom."
It consists of very few syllables yet possesses great merit;
by the mere hearing of it, all sentient beings will exhaust all karmic obscurations and will certainly become destined for enlightenment.
And those beings who are engaged in the accomplishment of mantras, their mantras will be accomplished without obstacles.
Then the Blessed One gave his approval to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Āryāvalokiteśvara, the Great Compassionate One, saying: "Excellent, excellent, noble son!
You who have long been dedicated to the welfare, benefit, happiness, and supreme good of all sentient beings. Therefore, noble son, listen."
Pay close and careful attention;
I shall speak to you the Perfection of Wisdom in few syllables yet of great merit,
by the mere hearing of which all sentient beings will exhaust all their karmic obscurations.
They will certainly be destined for enlightenment;
and those beings who are engaged in the accomplishment of mantras, their mantras will be accomplished without obstacles.
Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara said this to the Blessed One: "Therefore, O Sugata, please speak for the sake, the benefit, and the happiness of all sentient beings.
Thereupon, at that time, the Blessed One entered the meditative absorption named 'Liberation from All Suffering.
And as the Blessed One had entered that meditative absorption, hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of light rays issued forth from the opening of the circle of hair between his eyebrows.
And by those rays, all buddha-fields were completely illuminated;
and whatever beings were touched by that light,
they all became destined for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
As far as the beings in the hells [were concerned], all the Buddha-fields shook in six ways,
and divine rains of sandalwood powder fell at the feet of the Tathāgata.
Then, at that time, the Blessed One spoke the perfection of wisdom as follows: "A bodhisattva mahāsattva should possess an even mind;
he should possess a mind of loving-kindness toward all sentient beings."
One should be grateful and one should be mindful of benefits received;
one should have a mind that abstains from all evil.
And this Heart of the Perfection of Wisdom should be taken up: Homage to the Triple Gem!
Homage to Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One!
It is as follows: Oṃ mune mune mahāmunaye svāhā!
By the attainment of this perfection of wisdom, I have realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;
and all Buddhas have emerged from it.
I too have heard this very Prajñāpāramitā directly from the Tathāgata Mahāśākyamuni.
Therefore, you have been prophesied for Buddhahood at the head of all bodhisattvas: "Young man, in a future time, you shall become [Samantaraśmisamu]..."

There has appeared a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One, named Śrīkūṭarāja. [Is this not so?]

Those who shall hear this name, uphold it, recite it, cause it to be written, and extensively proclaim it to others; and having even committed it to writing, shall keep it in their homes and honor it—
All of them shall become Tathāgatas through little means and little hearing.
It is as follows: Oṃ jeya jeya padmābhe avame avame sarasaraṇi dhiridhiri devatā anupālani yuddhottāriṇi paracakranivāriṇi pūraya pūraya bhagavati all the hopes of myself and of all sentient beings!
Purify all karmic obscurations;
[blessed] by the Buddhas, svāhā!
This, noble son, is that ultimate Perfection of Wisdom, the mother of all Buddhas, the mother of Bodhisattvas (the giver of enlightenment),
and the remover of evil.
Even all the Buddhas together would not be able to describe its benefits, even in hundreds of millions of eons.
By the mere recitation of this, one becomes consecrated within all mandalas of the assembly,
and all mantras become manifest before one.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Āryāvalokiteśvara said this to the Blessed One: "For what reason, Blessed One, is this Perfection of Wisdom so few in syllables?
The Blessed One replied: "Because it is of little means;
even those beings who have dull tastes [are reached by it]."
They too shall uphold, recite, write, and cause to be written this Perfection of Wisdom in its few syllables;
all of them, by means of a small expedient, shall become intent upon awakening. For this reason, noble son, this Perfection of Wisdom is abbreviated and consists of few syllables.
When this had been said, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara spoke thus to the Blessed One: "It is marvelous, Blessed One;

it is most marvelous, Sugata, that the Blessed One has spoken this Dharma-discourse for the sake of the welfare of all beings, and for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of those who are dull-witted."
Thus spoke the Blessed One.
The noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
those monks, those Bodhisattvas, and the entire assembly— including the world of gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas— rejoiced and highly praised what the Blessed One had said.
The Perfection of Wisdom in Few Syllables is completed.
